title: Procedural Planet & Terrain Builder
description: I built a procedural planet and terrain generator as a weekend project for the LibGDX generation of Bridge Captain. Using fractal and Perlin-noise techniques, the tool generated configurable color terrain maps and grayscale heightmaps, supported seamless tiled output, created lakes and plateaus through adjustable terrain shaping, and produced assets that I continued using later in the Unity/VR versions of the game.

sections.title: Built for Bridge Captain
paragraphs: I originally built the tool to generate planetary surfaces for the LibGDX generation of Bridge Captain.
Although it started as a small weekend project, the generated planet assets remained useful enough that I continued using the same approach later when Bridge Captain moved into Unity and VR.

sections.title: Procedural Terrain Generation
paragraphs: The generator used fractal and Perlin-noise techniques to create synthetic terrain rather than relying entirely on hand-authored planet textures.
The same core algorithm could produce very different worlds by changing terrain-shaping parameters and the color palette supplied to the generator.

sections.title: Configurable Planet Styles
paragraphs: The tool accepted a list of colors that were mapped across the generated terrain values. Changing that palette allowed the same procedural system to create visibly different planet types.
items: Different planet appearances from the same generator

sections.title: Terrain Shaping Controls
paragraphs: I exposed controls for shaping the character of the generated terrain rather than producing only one fixed noise pattern.

sections.title: Heightmaps & Shadow Casting
paragraphs: The generator could also output a grayscale version of the terrain. I used this as a heightmap for calculating and casting shadows across the generated planetary surface.
This let the procedural terrain contribute to the final visual treatment rather than serving only as a texture source.

sections.title: Seamless Tiled Terrain
paragraphs: I built a fractal version that tiled perfectly, allowing opposite edges of the generated terrain to match seamlessly.
This was useful for surfaces that needed to repeat without obvious seams.

sections.title: Continuous Noise Sampling
paragraphs: The underlying procedural algorithm was not limited to one fixed image and could be sampled continuously across coordinates, making it suitable in principle for infinite terrain generation.
I did not build a chunked infinite-terrain system as part of this editor, so I keep that distinction separate from the later voxel-engine work.

sections.title: Animated & Displaced Terrain Effects
paragraphs: I also reused the procedural field for animated effects such as lava and manipulated the generated depth/displacement to produce different planetary surface treatments.

sections.title: Used Across Engine Generations
paragraphs: The output from this tool was used in the Bridge Captain LibGDX version and continued into the later Unity/VR generation.
That made the generator a reusable production tool rather than a one-off procedural-noise experiment.

sections.title: Separate Voxel Evolution
paragraphs: I later used 3D Perlin noise in a separate voxel-engine project, where the problem expanded into chunked volumetric generation. That work was a different system and is kept separate from this planet-builder card.

historicalNotes: The exact date is not source-anchored. Approximately 2014 is used because Jamie remembers building the tool around the Bridge Captain LibGDX generation, after the 2012 C.E.L.L./Android release and before the 2015 Unity/VR work.
This was a solo weekend project.
The tool was originally created to generate planets for Bridge Captain LibGDX.
The same procedural approach and generated assets continued to be used in later Unity/VR Bridge Captain work.
The tool generated both colored terrain and grayscale heightmaps.
The grayscale output was used for height-based shadow casting.
Remembered controls include roughness, plateau shaping for lakes/lake beds, and the angle used for shadow casting.
The generator accepted configurable color lists/palettes to create different planet appearances.
Jamie built a fractal implementation that tiled perfectly.
The editor itself did not implement chunked terrain streaming.
The underlying algorithm could be sampled continuously and was suitable in principle for infinite terrain, but Jamie did not ship an infinite-terrain system using this editor.
Jamie animated the procedural field for effects such as lava.
Jamie also used depth/Z displacement to create different planetary treatments.
Later 3D Perlin-noise chunking belonged to a separate voxel-engine project and should not be conflated with this tool.

The original portfolio description said the tool created both tileable and infinite terrain. Public wording should be more conservative: seamless tiled generation was implemented, while continuous sampling made infinite terrain possible in principle but a chunked infinite-terrain implementation was not shipped in this project.
